record.paper_title: On two open problems about embedding of modules in free modules
record.original_question: For a ring R, call R a left FGF ring when each finitely generated module over R on the left side can be injected into some free left R-module. Must every left FGF ring be Quasi-Frobenius?

evidence.quote: Is a left FGF ring Quasi-Frobenius?

artifact.self_contained_problem: A ring $R$ (associative, with identity) is called a left FGF ring if every finitely generated left $R$-module embeds as a submodule of some free left $R$-module. A ring $R$ is called quasi-Frobenius (QF) if $R$ is left (equivalently, right) artinian and left (equivalently, right) self-injective. Determine whether every left FGF ring is necessarily quasi-Frobenius.
artifact.status_search_result: The FGF conjecture — asking whether every (left) FGF ring is quasi-Frobenius — is a well-known long-standing open problem due to Faith. It has been confirmed under many additional hypotheses (e.g., left noetherian, semilocal with essential left socle, left self-injective, right CF, right Kasch), but the general question remains open as of recent surveys and papers on the topic.

status_evidence.title: When self-injective rings are QF: a report on a problem
status_evidence.snippet: Report on the FGF and related Faith conjectures about when self-injective rings are QF.
status_evidence.claim: Survey treats the FGF conjecture as an outstanding open problem with partial results.

status_evidence.title: New characterizations of pseudo-Frobenius rings and a generalization of the FGF conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: A generalization of the FGF conjecture is studied.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work continues to treat the FGF conjecture as open and seeks generalizations.

status_evidence.title: The FGF conjecture and the singular ideal of a ring
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the FGF conjecture via the singular ideal.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms FGF conjecture is still being investigated, supporting open status.
